'''Igor Konstantinovich Svanidze''' ({{lang-ka|იგორ კონსტანტინეს ძე სვანიძე}}; 31 August 1926 – 30 January 2018), who published as '''I. K. Svanidze''', was a Georgian [[Neurohistology|neurohistologist]] and [[Neuroscience|neurobiologist]]. He founded and headed the Laboratory of Neuromorphology at the [[Beritashvili Institute of Physiology]] in [[Tbilisi]] and taught [[Cell biology|cytology]] and [[histology]] at [[Tbilisi State University]] for more than four decades. He is credited with introducing the [[Tissue culture|culture of nervous tissue]] to Georgia and was among the country's first researchers in neurohistochemistry, working together with [[Alexander I. Roitbak|Alexander Roitbak]].<ref name="nplg" /><ref name="eminent" />

== Early life and education ==
Svanidze was born on 31 August 1926.<ref name="nplg" /> He grew up in Tbilisi and studied at Tbilisi State University, graduating from the Department of Biology in 1951. He later received the degrees of [[Candidate of Sciences]] and [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Biological Sciences]].<ref name="nplg" /><ref name="iliauni" />

== Career ==
Svanidze taught in the Department of Cytology, Histology and Embryology of the Faculty of Biology at Tbilisi State University from 1959 to 2006, where he lectured on cytology and pathological histology and gave a special course in pathological histology for master's students.<ref name="eminent" />

At the Institute of Physiology of the [[Georgian National Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences of the Georgian SSR]], later named after [[Ivane Beritashvili]], he founded a Laboratory of Histochemistry in 1967.<ref name="eminent" /> He later founded and headed the institute's Laboratory of Neuromorphology. He continued research at the institute, by then the Ivane Beritashvili Center of Experimental Biomedicine, until his death.<ref name="biomed2018" />

Over his career he supervised several doctoral and candidate dissertations.<ref name="eminent" />

== Research ==
Svanidze's early work concerned quantitative changes in protein functional groups and [[nucleic acid]]s in [[neuron]]s and [[glia|glial cells]] during development and under increased functional activity, the subject of his 1974 monograph on nucleic acids in the [[Pyramidal cell|pyramidal cells]] of the [[cerebral cortex]].<ref name="eminent" /><ref name="nplg" /> He also identified [[Monosynaptic reflex|monosynaptic]] pathways linking the [[retina]] to the [[visual cortex]] and other brain regions.<ref name="eminent" />

He introduced [[Organotypic culture|organotypic]] and dissociated cultures of nervous tissue to Georgia.<ref name="eminent" /><ref name="biomed2018" /> Using these methods he studied [[Neuromuscular junction|neuromuscular connections]] and types of [[axon]] growth, the role of contacts between cells in [[protein synthesis]], and the reconstruction in dissociated culture of a structure analogous to the [[claustrum]].<ref name="eminent" /><ref name="biomed2018" /> His 1981 monograph summarized this work.<ref name="nplg" />

Other research topics included the differentiation and repair of [[central nervous system]] (CNS) cells during [[ontogeny|ontogenesis]] and in disease, and the stimulation of recovery after CNS injury by pharmacological and physical factors.<ref name="iliauni" /> With the Centre of Experimental and Clinical Medicine of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] he studied changes in central nerve cells under acute [[Hypoxia (medical)|hypoxia]].<ref name="biomed2018" /> He also studied the function of the [[cilium|cilia]] of [[Ependyma|ependymal cells]] lining the [[cerebral aqueduct]], including the effects of weakened and strengthened [[magnetic field]]s on them.<ref name="eminent" />

In his later years Svanidze's laboratory studied the effects of [[Prenatal development|prenatal]] exposure to [[ethanol]] and [[toluene]] on [[neurogenesis]], metabolism and behavior in the [[Limbic system|limbic]] and [[Motor system|motor systems]] of rats, and the protective effect of [[antioxidant]]s. The work found that such exposure reduced the proliferation of ependymal [[stem cell]]s and of [[progenitor cell]]s in the [[dentate gyrus]] of offspring, disrupted neuronal and glial migration, and reduced exploratory activity, findings the group linked to [[fetal alcohol spectrum disorder|fetal alcohol]] and [[fetal toluene syndrome|toluene syndromes]].<ref name="eminent" /> His last project, funded by the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation from 2015 to 2018, examined the stimulating effect of low ([[Hormesis|hormetic]]) doses of ethanol on limbic neurogenesis.<ref name="eminent" />

== Honours and memberships ==
* [[Order of Honor (Georgia)|Order of Honor]]<ref name="nplg" /><ref name="biomed2018" />
* Honored Scientist of Georgia<ref name="nplg" /><ref name="biomed2018" />
* [[Open Society Foundations|Soros Foundation]] science prize (1993)<ref name="nplg" /><ref name="eminent" />
* Full member of the [[New York Academy of Sciences]] (1996)<ref name="eminent" />
* Member of the [[International Brain Research Organization]], the [[Federation of European Neuroscience Societies]] and [[Sigma Xi]]<ref name="eminent" /><ref name="iliauni" />

== Selected works ==
Svanidze was the author of more than 100 scientific papers, as well as monographs and textbooks.<ref name="eminent" /><ref name="nplg" /><ref name="pubmed" />
